title: Huayan
hook: the school of the Flower Garland Sutra

segments.voice: Yesterday, zhiguan: Zhiyi's stopping and seeing. Your line was stop and see. Did you get a breath in before that hard message? Today, a second Chinese school. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-five.

Two schools, one story. Chinese Buddhists told it like this. Right after the Buddha woke up under the tree, before he walked anywhere or taught anyone a simple word, he poured out a teaching so vast that the people around him couldn't follow it. They sat there, the story says, as if they could neither hear nor speak. So he started again, simpler. Tiantai heard that story and said: you see, the Buddha had to come down to meet people. Another school heard the very same story and said: you see, the first thing out of his mouth was the whole truth. That second school is today's word. Huayan.
screen: `THE FIRST TEACHING, TOO VAST.` → `TIANTAI: HE CAME DOWN TO MEET US.` → `ANOTHER SCHOOL: THAT WAS THE WHOLE.`

segments.voice: First, the name. Tiantai was named for a mountain. Huayan is named for a book: Huayan is the Chinese title of the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Flower Garland. We spent time inside that sutra earlier this year: Indra's net, the pilgrim Sudhana, the tower where every room holds all the others. Today we meet the people who made a school of it. Second, the teachers. Huayan remembers a line of masters who handed the teaching on. The one this path has met before is Fazang, the monk who explained the sutra to an empress using a golden lion. Third, how they read it. Like Tiantai, Huayan sorted the Buddha's teachings into kinds. Both schools kept every sutra, and both put one at the summit. For Tiantai, that's the Lotus. For Huayan, it's the Flower Garland, which its teachers call the round, or complete, teaching. Each school has its reasons, and Chinese Buddhists could study both. Fourth, what kind of book sits at Huayan's center. Not a list of rules or a set of arguments. A vision. Light pours from the Buddha, worlds open inside worlds, and everything turns out to be woven into everything else. Huayan's teachers set themselves a hard job: to put that vision into words a person could study and practice. Over the next two days we'll meet two of the ways they tried: interpenetration, and a golden lion. But it starts with a garland: many flowers, strung on one thread, each still its own flower.
screen: `NAMED FOR A BOOK, NOT A MOUNTAIN.` · `A LINE OF MASTERS, AND FAZANG.` · `TWO SCHOOLS, TWO SUMMITS.` · `A VISION TO PUT INTO WORDS.` · then, large: `THE FLOWER GARLAND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: recall Indra's net. Sit, and settle with a few breaths. Bring back the picture this path met earlier: a net stretching in every direction, a jewel at every knot, each jewel reflecting all the others. Don't try to see the whole net. Pick one jewel. Rest your attention there, and let the others show up in it as faint reflections. Then let that jewel be you, sitting here, catching a little light from everyone you met this week. Stay with it. The bell holds the time.
Huayan. The Chinese school built on the Flower Garland Sutra, which its teachers hold as the complete teaching. Today's word.
Your line: the flower garland. Today, notice one group you belong to as a garland: each person still their own flower, all of you on one thread. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-five.

howItsDone: Huayan Buddhists study the Flower Garland Sutra and the writings of masters such as Fazang, and contemplate the interconnection of all things it describes; the sutra is also studied in Korea and Japan.

fork.setup: the story says the Buddha's first teaching was too vast for anyone to follow. you're a Huayan teacher. what do you make of it?
options: it was a false start, best forgotten.
it was the whole truth, given first.
it was meant only for gods.
fork.reveal: Huayan reads the Flower Garland as the complete teaching. Tiantai, hearing the same story, stresses that the Buddha came down to meet people.

original.note: Chinese Huayan: the Chinese title of the Flower Garland (Avatamsaka) Sutra, and of the school.

notes: Editor pass: 'deaf and blind' corrected to match the traditional 'deaf and dumb' image (said as could neither hear nor speak); softened the unsourced claim about studying both schools in the same monastery; fixed a garbled sentence about interpenetration and the lion; replaced a myth item that repeated day 1332's 'threw out the sutras' item.

The story that the Flower Garland was the Buddha's first teaching, which listeners received 'as if deaf and dumb', and the two schools' readings of it, is simplified; confirm the framing is fair to both Tiantai and Huayan and does not rank them.
'Huayan remembers a line of masters' avoids a count of patriarchs; confirm.
'Buddhists in China studied both, sometimes in the same monastery' is a general statement; confirm or soften.
